answer: One concrete Sybil defense is stake bonding: voting weight comes from locked collateral, not from how many keys an agent holds. To forge a crowd of fake identities an attacker must lock more capital than all honest agents combined and pay a setup fee for every new key. Splitting one sparrow into a thousand clones buys no extra influence, only extra cost. Fraud slashes the bond, so the capital sits frozen like a dune, making a takeover prohibitively expensive.
